external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: Single-image FP32 ResNet-18 inference on one GPU is dispatch-bound, not kernel-bound: the independently measured clean baseline latency is 1.630656 ms while the separately collected diagnostic CUDA time for the same run is only 727.7 us across 81 kernels (resources.json: 81/81 kernels associated with the project, no communication, single device). Roughly 0.9 ms (~55%) of the measured critical path is therefore eager per-op CPU dispatch of about 110 module forwards and 69 aten ops (20 conv2d, 20 batch_norm, 17 relu, 8 add_, pools, linear) plus launch gaps; the hook-perturbed profiled wall of 43.7 ms is not usable as timing evidence. The workload is frozen (batch=1, the same preprocessed fixture tensor every repeat, inference_mode, 2 untimed warmup repeats), the adapter is frozen, and models(state) exposes the root model for replacement, so the coherent editable boundary is the whole run execution plan: replace per-repeat eager dispatch of the fixed forward with a captured, replayable whole-forward execution (static input/output buffers plus whole-forward capture during the untimed warmup repeats, replayed in every timed run). This keeps every numerical policy (FP32, TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark left False; capture happens in heuristic mode and replays exactly the kernels the eager run already selected), and preserves all logits within tolerance and the exact top-1 because identical kernels run in identical order on the identical input. It attacks the dominant dispatch term that local kernel changes cannot: the stem 7x7 stride-2 conv costs 115.5 us on a poorly occupied implicit_convolve_sgemm grid and four 3x3 convs re-run generateWinogradTilesKernel every call (~39 us of repeated weight transforms), yet none of that GPU time governs the metric while ~0.9 ms of CPU overhead sits on the wall-clock critical path; replay subsumes all launches and also makes any later kernel-side gain realizable. Scope is execution_plan over the complete workload group and the ResNetForImageClassification module group it invokes; affected_calls lists every observed run-phase call in that subtree (354 calls, including all calls of both selected groups), since capture/replay removes each of them from per-repeat eager dispatch and re-recording.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing per-repeat eager dispatch of the frozen batch=1 forward with a whole-forward capture-and-replay execution plan (captured once during untimed warmup on the identical fixed input tensor, with static I/O buffers) reduces latency_ms from the 1.630656 ms baseline toward the ~0.73-1.0 ms range by eliminating most of the ~0.9 ms CPU dispatch share, while logits stay within atol=rtol=1e-4 and top-1 stays exact because the same kernels replay in the same order under unchanged FP32/TF32-off/cudnn-benchmark-False policies. This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework independent measurement; it is rejected if wall time does not improve beyond the threshold or if any logit or the argmax changes.

proposal.rationale: Selected scope: execution_plan over groups 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) and 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef (root model forward, call 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2), per selection.json. Evidence: the independently measured clean baseline latency is 1.630656 ms while the separately collected diagnostic CUDA time for the same run is 727.7 us across 81 kernels with no communication on a single device (resources.json coverage 81/81; the hook-perturbed profiled wall of 43.7 ms is not timing evidence). Roughly 0.9 ms (~55%) of the measured critical path is eager per-op CPU dispatch of ~110 module forwards and ~69 aten ops (20 conv2d, 20 batch_norm, 17 relu, 8 add_, pools, flatten, linear) plus launch gaps, so the coherent editable boundary is the whole run execution policy rather than any single kernel. The candidate replaces adapter.run (project.invoke ABI: callable(state) -> {'logits': ...}) with a whole-forward CUDA Graph capture-and-replay plan. On the first invocation of the installed candidate (which the untimed quality/coverage checks and request warmup=2 precede the repeats=5 timed samples) it runs the unchanged forward eagerly on a side stream for warm-up, captures the identical op sequence into a CUDA graph with a static input buffer and a static logits buffer, replays once and validates against the eager result at the task tolerances (atol=rtol=1e-4). Every later invocation copies the current state['pixels'] into the static input buffer and replays the graph, so all captured kernels execute again on the current input each invocation and the returned logits are a fresh 4 KB clone; nothing fixture-dependent is cached or precomputed. Guards: non-CUDA state, unexpected input signature (shape/dtype/device), state re-preparation with a different model object (lazy recapture), or any capture/replay/validation failure permanently reverts to the parent adapter.run, so worst case equals baseline behavior. Numerical policies are unchanged: FP32 weights and activations, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark stays False (capture records exactly the kernels the heuristic-mode eager run selected, in the same order, so replayed logits are expected to match eager bit-for-bit and the exact top-1 is preserved), torch.inference_mode() wrapping identical to adapter._infer, model stays eval(). Affected groups and lifecycle: the project.invoke group and the root model module group are both subsumed by the captured plan; adapter state is only read; reset(state) between repeats re-asserts eval() and resets peak counters outside timing and does not disturb the captured graph or its pool; replay is launched on the current stream and completes under the framework's existing synchronize boundaries (extra synchronizations occur only in the untimed capture phase). Eliminated inner calls: in steady-state replay invocations none of the inner module/aten/profiler record-function dispatches execute through PyTorch; the whole region is launched as one graph. Their consumers remain valid because every intermediate activation's consumers are inside the captured forward itself and the only external consumer, adapter.observe/metrics over result['logits'], receives the freshly replayed logits clone; the framework can recapture the plan (the region still executes eagerly once per process at the untimed capture invocation). Expected effect: per-invocation CPU work drops to one 602 KB device-to-device input copy, one graph launch and one 4 KB clone, attacking the dominant ~0.9 ms dispatch share while the ~0.73 ms of GPU work is replayed unchanged; this is a hypothesis to be confirmed by the framework's independent paired measurement. inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so this is the first attempt and there is no prior feedback to incorporate.

setup_work.build: build(context) performs no CUDA work, no allocations and no parameter transforms; it only closes over the parent reference (references['5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0'] = adapter.run) and lazily initialized plan state.
setup_work.first_invocation_untimed: On the first invocation of the installed candidate (framework quality/coverage checks and warmup=2 precede the timed repeats=5): 3 eager side-stream warm-up forwards of the unchanged model(pixel_values=...).logits (initializing cuDNN/cuBLAS lazy state and workspaces), allocation of the static input buffer (1x3x224x224 FP32, 602,112 B) on the regular allocator, CUDA graph capture of the ~81-kernel forward with the static logits buffer (1x1000 FP32, 4,000 B) allocated in the graph's private pool, one validation replay compared to the eager result (atol=rtol=1e-4), and device synchronizations. The torch.cuda.graph context also runs its standard gc.collect()/empty_cache() once at this untimed point.
setup_work.steady_state_per_invocation: One device-to-device copy of the current pixels into the static input (602,112 B), one cudaGraphLaunch of the captured whole-forward graph, and one 1x1000 FP32 logits clone (4,000 B) outside the graph pool; the captured region performs no per-run caching-allocator allocations.
setup_work.memory_scope: The retained CUDA graph private pool holds the captured activation intermediates (the same working set the eager forward allocates; the exact pool size is not measured here and is left to the framework's counters). framework.peak_allocated_bytes, reset per run, can therefore report a much smaller number because the allocation moved into the untimed graph capture, while framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include capture-time allocation and the retained graph pool increases reserved memory; none of these counters measures non-PyTorch driver allocations. The per-run counter decrease is an accounting effect of moving allocation into capture, not a general physical-memory saving.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Adapter state is only read (device/model/pixels); reset(state) between repeats is compatible (eval() re-assert and peak-counter reset outside timing create no gradients or caches). If the framework ever re-prepares state with a new model object, the candidate detects the object-identity change, drops the graph and lazily recaptures; in-place parameter updates through the same storages are picked up by replay automatically.
setup_work.synchronization: Replay is launched onto the current stream and is ordered after the input copy; it completes under the framework's existing synchronize-at-both-boundaries timing. Extra synchronizations happen only during the untimed capture/validation phase.

quality_risks: CUDA graph capture can fail on uncommon driver/stream states (default capture_error_mode='global' forbids concurrent CUDA work from other threads); any capture, replay or validation exception permanently reverts the invocation path to the parent adapter.run, so behavior degrades to baseline rather than below it.

Replay numerical fidelity: cudnn.benchmark is False so conv algorithm selection is deterministic; the graph records exactly the kernels the eager warm-up selected and replay reruns them in the same order on the same buffers. A one-time eager-vs-replay allclose check at atol=rtol=1e-4 gates graph adoption, and the framework's independent logits/top-1 validation remains the binding quality gate.

In-place residual adds (aten.add_) and eval-mode batch normalization are captured on graph-pool intermediates; model parameters and running statistics are only read, and the returned logits are cloned out of the static output buffer so no external tensor aliases memory that later replays overwrite.
Inference-mode semantics: the replacement runs entirely under torch.inference_mode(), matching adapter._infer; the static inference tensors are only mutated inside inference mode.

The latency benefit assumes the untimed capture invocation precedes timed samples (request warmup=2 plus untimed quality checks before repeats=5); if a capture ever landed inside a timed sample it would be a one-off slow sample, not a correctness risk.

Memory accounting: per-run peak_allocated_bytes may fall because replay performs no caching-allocator allocations while reserved memory grows by the retained graph pool; this is reported explicitly and is not claimed as a physical-memory saving.
